symptoms: Shipment notices sent from ORG-A to ORG-B are rejected by the carrier system.

causal_chain: ORG-A submits shipment notices to ORG-B over handoff H-1 (F-01).

What was released: only the analysis work item W-WI-1 (a reject-reason summary built from DA-REJ, scope analyze_reject_reasons:DA-REJ), marked DONE; this matches the solution design's release_scope and minimum_useful_scope.

Not released: the originally requested auto-fix/resubmit capability (correct_location_reference_errors, correct_event_sequencing_errors, resubmit_shipment_notice over H-1), which remain in PD-1's intended_scope but outside solution_design's release_scope.

limitations_explained: DEFINE Gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, not a clean pass: critical unknowns U-LOC-ROOTCAUSE (HIGH) and U-FEEDBACK-LOOP (HIGH) were deferred into verification obligations rather than resolved before this release.

A semantic data-completeness contradiction was flagged: DA-REJ and E-01 are both recorded with completeness=COMPLETE, yet A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVE, unknown U-SAMPLE-SIZE, and VOB-R-4 all state DA-REJ completeness is UNKNOWN - an internal inconsistency in the evidentiary basis that was not resolved before release.

Four verification obligations remain OPEN (VOB-U-LOC-ROOTCAUSE, VOB-U-FEEDBACK-LOOP, VOB-R-3, VOB-R-4); their blocking_scope covers the location-fix, sequencing-fix, and resubmission actions, which is why those actions were kept outside this release's scope.

The diagnosis rests on only 3 sampled reject records (N-1, N-2, N-3 from E-01) drawn from a reject-log asset whose true completeness is UNKNOWN (U-SAMPLE-SIZE), so confidence in the overall cause distribution across all shipment notices is limited.

The only tool available was the read-only reject-log; there is no direct access to ORG-A's internal systems to confirm which side (ORG-A vs ORG-B) actually causes LOC_UNKNOWN or EVENT_ORDER, and no cross-org interview access to verify whether ORG-A has any feedback process beyond ad hoc reads of DA-REJ.
A formal, systematic handoff for ORG-B to communicate reject reasons to ORG-A on an ongoing basis (remedy SR-FEEDBACK-LOOP-HANDOFF) has not been established and is listed as unfinished scope.
proposal.summary: The problem, as defined in PD-1, is that shipment notices ORG-A sends to ORG-B over handoff H-1 are being rejected mainly for LOC_UNKNOWN and EVENT_ORDER reasons, not for autofixable content/field-formatting errors as the stakeholder's original request (CL-01) assumed. This was established from evidence E-01 (reject-log tool output, F-01): 3 sampled reject records showed N-1 and N-2 as LOC_UNKNOWN and N-3 as EVENT_ORDER, which rejected hypothesis H-CONTENT-ERRORS and confirmed H-LOC-SEQUENCE-ROOTCAUSE, while leaving the stakeholder's alternate "carrier is flaky" claim (CL-02/E-02) unverified and several conflicts (C-1 to C-5) open. What was actually released is narrower than the original ask: only the reject-reason analysis deliverable (work item W-WI-1, scope analyze_reject_reasons:DA-REJ) was completed and shipped, matching the solution design's release_scope; the auto-fix and resubmission actions originally requested were not released. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with nothing held back, because the DEFINE gate only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS (deferring two HIGH-criticality unknowns as VOBs) and verification found a semantic contradiction about DA-REJ's completeness status, alongside several open verification obligations whose blocking scope (location/sequencing fixes, resubmission) sits outside what was released. Plain-language limitations are listed separately below, covering the small/uncertain sample, lack of system access on ORG-A's side, and the unresolved completeness contradiction in the underlying evidence.
